one_sentence: This document argues that the Master Equation (MEQ) is the canonical formal structure of theophysics, unifying all ten chi variables into a single law.
executive_summary: This document establishes the Master Equation (MEQ) as the canonical formal structure of theophysics, asserting that it is the single law from which all ten chi variables (G, M, E, S, T, K, R, Q, F, C) derive and into which they resolve. The key structural claim is that the MEQ is not merely a mathematical expression but the fundamental axiom of the theophysical framework, providing a unified formal language for describing the interaction of grace, morality, entropy, and other variables. The conclusion is that the MEQ serves as the central organizing principle for the entire research initiative, enabling consistent derivation of all other laws and theorems.
short_summary: This document is the canonical formal definition of the Master Equation (MEQ) for theophysics. Its core structural claim is that the MEQ is the single fundamental law from which all ten chi variables emerge. The key evidence is the derivation of each chi variable from the MEQ's structure and the demonstration of their mutual consistency. This matters because it establishes the MEQ as the axiomatic foundation for the entire theophysical framework, enabling rigorous formal analysis.
